tossups.text: This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for islets of langerhans. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this insulin-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The insulin is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in islets of langerhans.

tossups.text: These beings were described as practicing "Machiavellian" tactics in a book titled [these beings'] Politics by Frans de Waal. The Kasakela community of these beings broke out into a civil war that lasted four years. One of these beings whose name was a play-on-words of "Noam Chomsky" was raised by two human parents as part of a failed investigation into the proof of these animals' language acquisition capability. One of these beings was observed using stalks of grass to hunt through a technique called "termite fishing." The Gardner sisters raised one of these animals named Washoe, who supposedly was the first of her kind to learn ASL. Frodo and Goliath were part of a group of these animals studied at Gombe Stream National Park in Tanzania. For 10 points, name these primates who were the main subject of Jane Goodall's research.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for liver functions. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this liver-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The liver is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in liver functions.

tossups.text: In human anatomy, this structure is essential for gallbladder and bile. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this liver-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The liver is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in gallbladder and bile.

tossups.text: The number of a type of these values in an interval is bounded by Budan's theorem and counted by Sturm's theorem. A field F is algebraically closed if, for each element in F-bracket-x, one of these values is in F. A matrix is this type of value with respect to its characteristic equation via the Cayley-Hamilton theorem. The existence of a specific type of these values is guaranteed by the intermediate value theorem for odd-degree polynomials. The number of sign changes in a polynomial is used to count a specific type of these values via Descartes's rule of signs. If a quadratic's discriminant is non-negative, then it has a real one of these values. For 10 points, name these values that correspond to a function's x-intercepts.

Louis XIV is kidnapped and replaced by his fictional twin Philippe in this author's The Vicomte of Bragelonne. That work is the sequel to a novel by this author in which the protagonist's lover Constance is poisoned by a woman with a fleur-de-lis branded on her shoulder. The protagonist of another novel by this author is arrested before marrying Mercedes and meets the Abbe Faria while imprisoned at the Chateau d'If. This author created M'Lady de Winter, who is opposed by Athos, Porthos, Aramis, and D'Artagnan. For 10 points, name this author of The Count of Monte Cristo and The Three Musketeers.

In this author's second novel, Henry calls a group of Black men in a car "a public menace" for speeding without a license or insurance. Later, the protagonist of that novel is horrified to see him and her father attend a Citizens' Council meeting. That novel was published fifty-five years after this author's previous novel, and references Dill's life in Italy and Calpurnia's retirement from housekeeping. In this author's first novel, Boo Radley thwarts an attack on Jem and his sister after their father defended a man falsely accused of rape. For 10 points, name this author who created the characters Scout and Atticus Finch in To Kill a Mockingbird.

This character is likened to Hoagy Carmichael in the first novel in which he appears. In a short story, Major Dexter Smythe tells this character how he murdered his adoptive father, before he is killed by an octopus. In one novel, this character remarks "the bitch is dead now" after the suicide of another character, the namesake of a cocktail. In that novel, this character is tortured after winning a game of baccarat against the SMERSH operative Le Chiffre ("SHEEF-rh"), having been bailed out by Felix Leiter ("LYE-tuh") and betrayed by Vesper Lynd. For 10 points, name this fictional spy created by Ian Fleming who first appears in Casino Royale.

One character in this novel describes how her boyfriend Max dies with a film reel under his arm when his motorcycle is hit by a bus. Another character in this novel encounters a prophetic mongoose with golden eyes after two policemen who resemble Elvis nearly beat her to death in a field. Its main character is saved from death when he hits a freeway median planted with shrubbery after jumping off a turnpike bridge. This novel describes its main character's mother in its section "The Three Heartbreaks of Belicia Cabral," and introduces its main character in its opening chapter, "Ghetto Nerd at the End of the World." Its central family is afflicted by a fuku supposedly caused by Abelard's refusal to let his niece be raped by Trujillo. The title character of this 2007 novel receives his nickname after being mistaken for the author of The Importance of Being Earnest. For 10 points, name this novel about a Dominican boy growing up in New Jersey, written by Junot Diaz.
tossups.answer: Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao
acceptableAnswers: Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao
The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao

tossups.text: The peninsula containing this location, but not this location itself, was annexed along with Stonecutters Island in 1899. Jackie Pullinger wrote about treating addicts living in this location in Crack in the Wall. A park containing the Chess Garden and the Eight Floral Walks contains the remnants of this location's south gate. Groups like 14K and Sun Yee On flourished in this settlement, which was connected to a nearby pier by the Lung Tsun Stone Bridge. This site was informally governed by a Kaifong association. This site was located right next to the Kai Tak airport. The demolition of this site was planned for a few years before the 1997 handover. For 10 points, name this extremely dense, crime-ridden settlement in Hong Kong.

This planet's equator is home to an elevated region known as the Tharsis Bulge, which is located near the Valles Marineris (VALL-us mare-in-AIR-us). It was visited by the Viking probes and is home to the highest mountain in the Solar System, the extinct volcano Olympus Mons. This planet is orbited by two small moons named Deimos and Phobos. For 10 points, a network of naturally occurring "canals" is on what planet between Earth and Jupiter?

Note to players: Description acceptable. A spiral staircase in this building's chapel leads to an otherwise-empty room filled with stained jewelry and ancient gold covered in dust. After waking up in his bedroom instead of this building's dusty, moonlit women's quarters, a man notices his watch is still unwound. After a fellow traveler quotes Gottfried Bürger's Lenore when whispering "For the dead travel fast," that visitor to this building transfers carriages at Borgo Pass. Two horses are frightened to death on the trail to this building by the snowy apparitions of three sisters. Those sisters attack a visiting solicitor after he sneaks out of his room and witnesses this building's namesake crawling on its walls. Communion wafers are used to banish the owner of this mirrorless building from its grounds by Abraham Van Helsing. For 10 points, Jonathan Harker travels to Romania to visit what building that is home to a vampire?
acceptableAnswers: prompt on answers indicating Dracula’s home

tossups.text: Examples of these substances used in redox reactions include iron II complexes of phenanthroline ["fee-mam-throw-leen"] and bipyridine ["bi-peer-ih-deen"]. Calcein is a complexometric type of these substances used in chelations. Triarylmethane ["tri-ar-uhl-meth-ay-n"] dyes like cresol purple and bromothymol blue are examples of these used to detect the presence of carbon dioxide. One of the most commonly used of these substances named phenolphthalein ["fee-no-thay-leen"] turns pink under basic conditions and can be used to find the endpoint of a titration. For 10 points, name these substances that change color due to change in pH, exemplified by litmus paper.
acceptableAnswers: dye before mention by asking “What are these dyes used as?”

tossups.text: Formed by the junction of the Biya and Katun, the Nenets and Enets occupy the northern part of its basin. Just after meeting the Inya, a dam forms the Novosibirsk Resevoir, and hydroelectric power stations harness it at Oskemen and Bukhtarma. Its basin was claimed for the tsar by the Cossack folk hero Yermak in the 16th century, and its lower section was explored during the Great Northern Expedition. Its outlet is a namesake gulf in the Kara Sea, and its source lies in the Altai mountains. For ten points, name this great river of Asia, the seventh-longest in the world, which runs through Siberia west of the Yenisey.

This position is the first of the three ikkarim put forth by Joseph Albo. Al-Farabi updated an earlier philosopher's idea of emanationism to center around this position. One statement for this position notes how "a thing is said to be hotter" as it "more nearly resembles that which is hottest."To support this position, William Lane Craig uses an argument put forth by the kalām school of philosophy. A refutation by Gaunilo concerning a "lost island" was used against an argument for this position from the Proslogion. Contingency and the Unmoved Mover are two of the "five ways" arguing for this position in Thomas Aquinas' Summa Theologica. For 10 points, St. Anselm's ontological argument argues for what theological position rejected by atheists?
acceptableAnswers: accept answers relating that God created the universe
prompt on specific arguments like the kalām cosmological argument

tossups.text: Modern industrial syntheses of vitamin C involve a fermentation process using this molecule as a starting material. This molecule's less common L isomer cannot react with hexokinase; its D isomer reacts with the enzyme to form a compound containing a phosphate on carbon number 6. The Cori cycle involves the conversion of pyruvate into this molecule. It can also be used to form two equivalents of pyruvate, the starting material of the citric acid cycle. A dimer containing two of these molecules is called mannose while it also forms a long linear chain called glucagon. For 10 points, name this monosaccharide with formula C6H12O6, often referred to as blood sugar.

2. One type of this chemical turns a transparent violet if amino acids have been formed and is named the biuret type. Another example turns color between green and dark red depending on the amount of sugar in the solution, and is named the Benedict's type. The limiting type is the chemical that has the smallest ratio of the amount of moles present to the amount of moles needed for the reaction. For 10 points, name this type of substance that can determine to what extent another substance has been created or is used to help produce other substances.

In this work, the teenaged Asya asks Dyomka to kiss her breast. When his son visits him at this novel's titular location, the Party member Pavel Rusanov berates him for being too soft on a truck driver who lost a box of macaroni in a snowstorm. Like its author, the main character of this work has been exiled due to Article 58, which deals with counterrevolutionaries. The protagonist of this work is left sexually impotent because of his residence in the title place. At this novel's end, the protagonist leaves a letter for Vera Gangart and boards a train back to Ush-Terek. For 10 points, name this work in which Oleg Filimonovich Kostoglov seeks treatment at the titular facility, a novel by Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn.

This philosopher created the eirôneia style, which later became known as his "irony." Aristophanes describes this man teaching how to avoid repayment of debt and making fun of traditional gods in The Clouds. This man's eponymous method involves asking many questions and distilling the answer that one seeks and was called elenchus. Claiming that he has no wisdom in Apology, for 10 points, identify this main speaker of The Republic and other Platonic dialogues whose opposition to Athenian democracy led to his trial and eventual suicide.

The Krutzsch process produced about a ten percent aqueous solution of this compound, but was never commercialized. This compound is produced commercially by sending bubbles of air through a solution of anthracene, leading to the autoxidation of 2-alkyl anthrahydroquinone to a 2-alkyl anthraquinone. That process is known as the AO process and was invented by Riedl and Pfleiderer. This compound is found with ferrous salts in Fenton's reagent, and oxidizes sodium hypochlorite to give oxygen. A three percent aqueous solution of it is useful for treating minor wounds. It is broken down to oxygen and water by catalase. For 10 points, name this oxidizing agent with formula H2O2.

Shaw controversially saw Great Britain and Germany as equally responsible for World War I, and previously wrote this play showing the futility of war, featuring the Bulgarian Raina Petkoff and the soldier Captain Bluntschli.

After Shaw's death, Ronald Kingsley Read and others designed the phonetic Shavian alphabet to his specifications and published a version of this Shaw play in it.
